judged_text: The recurring-event delete sweep (`bookingToDelete.user.credentials.filter(...endsWith("_calendar")).map(...)` over updatedBookings) now sits inside the per-reference loop without being made reference-aware, so it executes once per calendar reference and still deletes only the first calendar reference of each remaining series booking. Cancelling a recurring COLLECTIVE booking with N calendar references runs the sweep N times (duplicate deleteEvent calls whose failures are swallowed by the surrounding catch) and never touches the non-first hosts' events for the remaining series bookings — those hosts' calendars keep orphaned events.

adjudication.rationale: In `handleCancelBooking.ts`, `bookingCalendarReference` was changed from a single ref (`find`) to an array (`filter`) and the deletion logic is now wrapped in `for (const reference of bookingCalendarReference)`. Inside the `credentialId` branch, the recurring-series delete sweep (`bookingToDelete.user.credentials.filter(...endsWith("_calendar")).map(...)` iterating `updatedBookings`) is executed for every reference, but it still uses `updBooking.references.find((ref) => ref.type.includes("_calendar"))`, i.e. it only deletes the first calendar reference per remaining booking. This both (a) repeats the sweep once per calendar reference (duplicate deleteEvent calls) and (b) fails to delete non-first hosts' calendar events for the series, leaving orphaned events. Errors during the sweep are caught and only logged, so duplicate failures can be swallowed.
